_about: The dashboard To-Do feed: a short, layman-readable daily checklist of curation work (for Sam) and engineering/pre-curation work (for Fable, the Claude session), rendered by cpl_todos.js as the 📋 To-Do button on every tab. Refreshed at every Rule-8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff (this file is the handoff distilled for the dashboard). Check-off state lives in each viewer's browser (localStorage) and resets when _as_of changes. Keep it SHORT — ≤ ~12 items; done items are deleted, not checked.
_as_of: 2026-07-14 · Session 115 (StarMagna) — merge/mint doctrine GRADUATED (now v0.8); batch-apply authorized; scenario-refinement loop humming
_status: The merge/mint doctrine passed its graduation gate. We re-tested it with a blind AI pass (sees only the doctrine + the courses, never the old answers): it reproduced Sam's fundamental 'combine vs keep separate' call 92% of the time on the 52 groups he'd walked, and re-merged the 3 credit/noncredit mirror pairs it was built to fix. The finer call sat at 87% — every miss was a spot where the doctrine has since gained a rule Sam's older answers predate. Sam then ruled on the two remaining forks: (1) same-college level pairs — Printing (both introductory) merges cleanly; Custodial 1/2 merges with a parenthetical '(1 and 2)' because the 0.5-unit rungs are competency pieces; (2) 'People Skills' in Management (broad, program course) stays separate from the freelancer/enrichment one. Those rulings became new doctrine rules (P-6 ratified, new P-1b) and take agreement to ~95%. The doctrine has GRADUATED (v0.7) — whole-worklist batch-apply is now authorized (it still runs through its own dry-run→review→apply gates). Sam then walked a second tiny batch of 3 scenarios and settled 3 more open questions (generic 'Topics in X' shells → one umbrella per subject; enrichment-noncredit merges when the learning matches a credit course; ladders cap at 3 rungs, consolidating extras in pairs). Doctrine is now v0.8. Big product signal from Sam: he'd stopped using the in-app merge-review panel because thousands of suggestions overwhelmed him — so the winning format is a SMALL curated batch (a few high-value forks at a time), not the firehose. Next: wave 4 (2,000 more multi-college courses, staged), the batch-apply itself, and a 'decisions that need you' curated queue.
